correctness.rationale: Bézout against the two root lines gives anticanonical degree >= d+m0 for any other nonexceptional curve; adjunction forces d=1, m0=0 and a crossing pair for a negative curve. The two root curves are disjoint. For disjoint selected (-1)-curves, the root Schur block is -2I+MM^t; a shared E0 makes the two-root block singular, while without E0 the two root conditions are independent. An invariant negative-definite support descends: for a ground-field ample A, solve (-M)b=(A·C_i)_i, where M is the support Gram matrix. The solution is strictly positive (a negative part would contradict positive definiteness and the nonpositive off-diagonal of -M; a zero coordinate contradicts the positive right side). P=A+sum b_i C_i is big nef, orthogonal exactly to the support, and P+c sum C_i has the required negative part. Coefficients are rational and invariant by uniqueness. The common point and pair partition force D8. The proposed field realizations work: rational axes give independent inner swaps, conjugate axes with two points over the quadratic field give pair exchange, and a genuine degree-four coordinate gives the four-cycle. Any triple among the four outer points contains two points on one axis, so cannot be an extra collinear triple. Independent exact rational-pivot Gram enumeration matches all five rows, every bivariate coefficient, the identical curve-cycle vectors with 17 vs 23 fixed supports, and the orbit-size multiplicities 5,6,31,10. The supplied incidence script prints bivariate coefficients rather than asserting each coefficient; that evidence is the saved snapshot and the independent coefficient-by-coefficient comparison, not the terminal marker.
residual_risks: Finite calculation establishes combinatorics for the specified resolution, not singular Weil-divisor chambers or all arithmetic forms of the two-node surface.
